fileQuotes.text: No cable stack is used; reading the catalogue's `"cable_machine"` equipment tag as referring to the double-handle cable attachment hooked under the bar shaft is the chosen interpretation (rather than verified catalogue provenance), and keeping the torso still throughout the pull and return comes from `ALL_300_MOTION_MAP.json`'s quiet-torso constraint (`"Quiet hinged torso"`), not from the two still photographs.

Keeping your trunk braced through the descent, push your hips back and knees out to sit back under control until you are seated on the box with your thighs parallel to the floor and your shins approximately vertical, feet planted. Pause on the box without bouncing while keeping your trunk braced, then drive upward off the box through your heels with whole-foot pressure to stand tall.

Use a dumbbell that cannot roll (hexagonal heads, or wedged) placed on the floor in front of a sturdy support that cannot move, check it is stable before stepping on, hold the support with both hands for balance, and stand with the ball of one foot on the dumbbell handle and the other foot lifted clear of the floor.

Inside a squat rack, place a stable bench set so the glutes touch it lightly at about thighs parallel behind you, rest a barbell across the top of your front shoulders with your arms crossed to grasp the bar and your upper arms slightly above parallel to the floor, and step back into a shoulder-width stance with the toes slightly pointed out.

Immediately drive the hips and knees forward to stand tall, letting the kettlebell swing forward and up on a long, straight arm to chest to shoulder height, the arm following the hip drive while you keep your shoulders square.

basis: 'Draft written from the public-domain free-exercise-db entry (Bent_Over_Two-Arm_Long_Bar_Row) and its two photographs, awaiting the owner. The catalogue\'s own text for this movement is a placeholder on a source hold.',

instructions: 'Set a parallel-height box behind you inside a power rack and loop a band from each sleeve of a barbell down to the base of the rack or heavy dumbbells secured on the floor. Step under the bar to set it across the back of your shoulders, unrack it with your trunk braced and your head facing forward, and stand in front of the box in a shoulder-width to slightly wider stance with your feet planted. Keeping your trunk braced through the descent, push your hips back and knees out to sit back under control until you are seated on the box with your thighs parallel to the floor and your shins approximately vertical, feet planted. Pause on the box without bouncing while keeping your trunk braced, then drive upward off the box through your heels with whole-foot pressure to stand tall.',

instructions: 'Use a dumbbell that cannot roll (hexagonal heads, or wedged) placed on the floor in front of a sturdy support that cannot move, check it is stable before stepping on, hold the support with both hands for balance, and stand with the ball of one foot on the dumbbell handle and the other foot lifted clear of the floor. Keeping the knee straight and the dumbbell still, lower the working heel toward the floor to get a full stretch of the calf. While the dumbbell stays still, lift the heel to rise on the ball of the foot over the handle into a full calf extension, contract the calf hard at the top, and hold for a second. Lower the heel under control back into the stretch while the dumbbell stays still, complete the repetitions, then change legs.',

instructions: 'Inside a squat rack, place a stable bench set so the glutes touch it lightly at about thighs parallel behind you, rest a barbell across the top of your front shoulders with your arms crossed to grasp the bar and your upper arms slightly above parallel to the floor, and step back into a shoulder-width stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keeping your head up, your back straight, and your elbows high, bend the knees tracking with the toes over a whole foot to lower slowly until your glutes lightly touch the bench at about thighs parallel. Do not sit back and relax on the bench. Push the floor through your heels over the whole foot to straighten the legs and return to standing tall.',

instructions: 'Set a kettlebell on the floor a short step ahead of your feet in a stance slightly wider than your hips, soften the knees and push the hips back with a flat back to grip the handle in one hand with an overhand grip, and hike the bell back between your thighs with the free arm swinging back beside your hip. Immediately drive the hips and knees forward to stand tall, letting the kettlebell swing forward and up on a long, straight arm to chest to shoulder height, the arm following the hip drive while you keep your shoulders square. Let the bell drop back down along the same arc and hinge at the hips as your hand passes your thighs to catch the backswing into the next repetition, then park the bell under control on the floor ahead of your feet at the end of the set before changing arms.',
